decision: Trim swarm-manager-backlog-tools CLI Commands section (~258 lines, ~3K tokens) into a pointer at 'swarm-manager <group> --help' plus a short list of non-obvious usage notes
rationale: Baseline: skill is 527 lines / 27,565 chars / ~6,900 tokens; the CLI Commands section alone is 258 lines / 12,286 chars / ~3,000 tokens (44% of skill). Loaded by 19 inbound consumers (catalog-strategist, portfolio-manager, vision-walk-prep, director-swarm, monetization, morning-vision-walk, 13 swarm-manager-* skills). Health 0.51 with a 'skill content is oversized' warning. The swarm-manager CLI already has self-documenting help: 'swarm-manager backlog --help' lists every subcommand with flags; same for initiatives / captures / stats / agent-manager. The prose section duplicates that surface verbatim and drifts whenever the CLI adds commands (e.g., backlog workshop-reset, search-ai, review-decide already present in --help but require re-editing the skill to stay in sync). Expected delta: replace CLI Commands section with a one-paragraph pointer + a 15-20-line 'non-obvious usage patterns' block (stdin heredoc for file-upload, batch --preview before --execute, referential-integrity-is-automatic note, initiatives context as single-call loader). Estimated post-trim skill size: ~4,400 tokens (down from ~6,900, a ~36% reduction of the whole skill, ~80% reduction of the CLI section). Per-read savings: ~2,500 tokens × 19 consumers = compounding savings every time any of those skills is loaded. Measurement plan: (1) re-count chars/tokens after edit and log delta in PROGRAMMATIC_CONVERSION_QUEUE.md; (2) re-run graph health and confirm the oversized-content warning drops; (3) spot-check one downstream skill (e.g., swarm-manager-workshop) still has enough surface to do its job by tracing its CLI calls against the new pointer + --help output; (4) 14-heartbeat revisit to check for drift regressions or consumer complaints.
notes: Accepted 2026-04-24 vision walk. CLI self-documents via --help; prose duplicates and drifts. Replace CLI Commands section with pointer + 15-20 line non-obvious-patterns block. Measurement plan per decision rationale: log delta in PROGRAMMATIC_CONVERSION_QUEUE.md, re-run graph health, spot-check one downstream skill, 14-heartbeat revisit.

decision: Add tier-1 verification gate to run-introspector HEARTBEAT.md so errored runs with exit_code=429 and substantive completion text are reclassified as tier-5 misclassified-success, not investigated as real failures
rationale: Run 60116710-f77d-4c33-8058-2bd90c475289 is itself a successful agent-manager investigation run whose final report text (which mentions 'rate limit' dozens of times as a topic) tripped detectRateLimit's substring match at scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/adapters/runner/claude_code.go:1518-1559, forcing ExitCode=429 on a clean exit. The report diagnoses its own misclassification (category Environment/Tooling, severity Critical) and names sibling false-positive e08357a4-87a9-4b16-b5ed-99c46aacc39d. Pattern verification: 2 of 22 FAILED runs (~9%) carry exit_code=429 + substantive markdown completion text rather than rate-limit banners, consistent with finding E1 in the run's own report. Without a tier-1 gate, run-introspector will keep picking these false positives as errored and drawing the wrong agent-behavior lessons. Proposed edit (team-agent-optimizer's lane): in scenarios/prompt-manager/store/teams/meta-optimization/members/run-introspector/HEARTBEAT.md 'Required Loop' step 3, after the ladder walk, add: 'If the candidate has exit_code=429 and error_msg is multi-paragraph / contains markdown headings (Summary, Classification, Report, etc.) rather than a rate-limit banner, skip as misclassified and continue the ladder.' This is an HEARTBEAT.md-only change — do not modify detectRateLimit itself (that is scenario-qa's lane on agent-manager code quality). Baseline: 2/22 false-positive rate today. Measurement: after edit, no future RUN_LESSONS.md entry should pick an exit_code=429-with-completion-text run as tier-1 errored. Revisit 2026-04-30 (7 heartbeats). In-lane check: proposes an agent-file edit by team-agent-optimizer (agent-improvement context), not a direct code change; fails neither sprawl, polishing, nor scope creep.
notes: Deferred, not disagreed. Revisit after 2026-05-01 (~7 heartbeats). detectRateLimit was recently addressed on the agent-manager side (scenario-qa lane); want to observe whether the underlying false-positive pattern (exit_code=429 + markdown completion text) still recurs before adding a redundant tier-1 gate in run-introspector HEARTBEAT.md. If run-introspector's own heartbeat continues to mis-pick such runs after 2026-05-01, it will naturally re-propose — which is the signal we want. Rejection here is a workaround for a missing 'deferred' status (captured as friction F12 — proper defer primitive to be filed as backlog item).

decision: Resolve gold-star reference rot on reference-react-vite: 72 standards violations (41 High) on first toolchain scan; reference cannot serve as the clean baseline until cleaned up
rationale: Reference-react-vite was accepted as gold-star reference on 2026-04-24 per dec-1776981723540926630. REFERENCE_SCENARIOS.md nomination rule 2 requires the reference to 'score clean on every current toolchain tool', and rule 4 requires structural stability for ≥60 days. The first real scan (job standards-18dd3de9-aa0b-4039-bdc5-61b09f65c7f6) returned 72 violations dominated by stack-governance (37 — Makefile structure/lifecycle missing canonical PHONY targets, lifecycle commands not calling vrooli scenario, header/color constants wrong), type-safety (6 — strict mode + noUncheckedIndexedAccess off in ui/tsconfig.json, ESLint typed config incomplete), quality-gates (4 — vite build skips tsc --noEmit; .vrooli/testing.json strict flags off for both node_package and go_module), go-quality (2 — no .golangci.yml in api/ or cli/), plus 17 ui-a11y-v1 missing focus-visible rules. tidiness-manager corroborates: make lint and make type both exit 2 because the .PHONY targets aren't defined. This is reference-rot per REFERENCE_SCENARIOS.md classification (the scenario hasn't drifted yet — it was never scanned-clean before nomination), so the operator action is to (a) clean up reference-react-vite to score zero High violations, or (b) demote it and re-nominate once clean. Until resolved, every other scenario being compared 'against the gold standard' is being compared against a dirty target. Many violations have auto-fix recipes — type-safety rules cite 'scenario-auditor fix <scenario> --rules TS_CONFIG_STRICT' as a one-shot remediation. Recommended sequence: (1) auto-fix tsconfig + eslint (TS_CONFIG_STRICT + ESLINT_TYPED_CONFIG); (2) regenerate Makefile from canonical template; (3) add api/.golangci.yml + cli/.golangci.yml; (4) add focus-visible CSS to interactive UI components; (5) re-run scan. Baseline: 72 violations / 41 High / 10 Medium / 20 Low / 1 Info. Target: 0 High, ≤5 Low. Do not touch reference-react-vite myself — that's outside toolchain-validator's lane (TEAM.md operating rule: 'Does NOT fix violations in the reference scenario').

decision: Toolchain triage is blocked by two gaps: (a) test-genie run-tests returns opaque HTTP 500 with no severity/category detail, and (b) development-toolchain-validator still does not implement validate/report subcommands despite a reference now existing
rationale: Both gaps are now consequential because a gold-star reference exists (reference-react-vite, dec-1776981723540926630). Until 2026-04-24 these were deferred 'no target to validate against'; now they directly hamper the heartbeat. Specifics: (a) test-genie run-tests reference-react-vite returns the literal string 'api error (500): scenario tests failed' — no severity, no failed-test list, no log handle. Toolchain-validator cannot categorize this into critical/major/minor or compare it across heartbeats. HEARTBEAT.md's documented verb 'test-genie run <reference>' does not exist either; the actual verb is 'run-tests'. (b) DTV CLI exposes only reference/connection/status/configure groups, but HEARTBEAT.md's 'Preferred (when available)' list includes 'validate <reference>' and 'report --conflicts | --drift | --maturity | --tool-baselines'. Without these, the fallback trio (scenario-auditor + test-genie + tidiness-manager) is the only path, with the opaque-500 problem above. This is a capability-gap (not a toolchain-violation) because the capability is missing, not regressed — the right consumer is director-swarm (which owns capability-gap discovery for new scenarios per TEAM.md cross-team boundaries). Suggested sub-gaps to backlog: (1) test-genie run-tests should return structured failure output (per-suite results, exit code, log artifact path); (2) DTV ships validate <reference> that wraps the trio and returns a unified violation report; (3) DTV ships report --conflicts/--drift/--maturity/--tool-baselines so toolchain-validator can compare scans across heartbeats programmatically. Baseline: today, the heartbeat needs ~6 separate CLI invocations and manual aggregation; with these capabilities it would be 1-2 invocations with structured output. Not raising as toolchain-violation — these are missing features, not broken ones. No prior pending capability-gap from this member to supersede.

decision: Edit run-introspector HEARTBEAT.md step 3 (Triage) to add a tier-1 false-positive verification gate for exit_code=429 runs whose error_msg is substantive task output rather than a rate-limit banner
rationale:
Baseline: RUN_LESSONS.md entry 2026-04-23 (run `60116710`) documents that run-introspector spent a heartbeat investigating a successfully-completed investigation run that was misclassified as FAILED/429 because its assistant report discussed 'rate limit' as a topic. The substring matcher `detectRateLimit` in `scenarios/agent-manager/api/internal/adapters/runner/claude_code.go:1518-1559` fires on any assistant text containing 'rate limit' regardless of IsError, forcing Success=false, ExitCode=429. Recent-failed-runs scan in that lesson confirms 2/22 (~9%) of FAILED runs match the pattern (ids `60116710`, `e08357a4`).

Current step 3 prose (run-introspector/HEARTBEAT.md): '3. **Triage.** Walk the ladder in order. At the first tier with a run not already in RUN_LESSONS.md, pick one. Stop walking the ladder.' This picks the contaminated tier-1 runs first every time they surface.

Proposed edit: replace step 3 with — '3. **Triage.** Walk the ladder in order. At the first tier with a run not already in RUN_LESSONS.md, pick one — but apply the **tier-1 false-positive gate** first: if the candidate is an errored run with exit_code == 429 AND the error_msg looks like substantive task output (multi-paragraph markdown with headings such as Summary / Classification / Report) rather than a terse rate-limit banner, reclassify it as tier-5 (random-success-with-misclassification), record the false-positive in RUN_LESSONS.md, and continue walking the ladder. Otherwise, stop walking. Rationale: detectRateLimit (claude_code.go:1518-1559) substring-matches "rate limit" anywhere in the final assistant message, so investigations whose reports merely discuss rate-limiting get misclassified — see RUN_LESSONS.md 2026-04-23 (`60116710`).'

Expected delta: tier-1 false-positive investigations drop from ~9% of picks to ~0%; ~1 wasted heartbeat per ~11 runs is recovered. Run-introspector still records the false-positive (so the misclassification rate stays measurable), but does not waste depth on it.

Measurement plan: (a) after merge, the next RUN_LESSONS.md entry that encounters a 429+substantive-text run should mark it 'tier-1 false-positive (skipped)' rather than open a full lesson on it; (b) grep RUN_LESSONS.md 7 heartbeats from now — count of tier-1 lessons opened on 429-completion-text runs should be 0; (c) when scenario-qa fixes detectRateLimit, the gate becomes a no-op (still correct, no rollback needed).

Failure-mode check: (1) not polishing — concrete documented misfire that already cost a heartbeat; (2) not sprawl — editing existing agent file, not adding entities; (3) not premature programmatic conversion — prose-to-prose edit, no scenario backing involved; (4) not churn-without-benefit — clear baseline + delta; (5) not too-fast deprecation — improve, not prune; (6) in-lane — team-agent-optimizer edits agent files (HEARTBEAT.md is part of run-introspector's prompt assembly); the underlying claude_code.go bug is explicitly NOT touched (that's scenario-qa); (7) not conversion-without-measurement — measurement plan above.

Visited tracker: knw-1777069883310471139. Audit snapshot: knw-1777069892849442354. Source handoff: RUN_LESSONS.md 2026-04-23 lesson 'Proposed change' paragraph and 'Handoff' line. No prior pending agent-improvement decisions on run-introspector to supersede.

decision: Edit run-introspector HEARTBEAT.md tier-3 (Slow) to define duration as work-duration (last_heartbeat - started_at), not wall-clock; exclude runs where resolved_config.requires_approval=true (or summary.turns_used<=1 AND cost_estimate<$0.20) from slow triage
rationale:
Baseline: 25 of 98 successful runs in this heartbeat's window are `swarm-manager:initiative:rev-trigger:review:round-001` with wall-clock 70k–82k seconds. Spot-check of `564191ef-e1b4-4328-b21c-c83999676123` (wall-clock 81,648s, the longest) shows `last_heartbeat - started_at = 15s`, `summary.turns_used=1`, `summary.tokens_used=27523`, `summary.cost_estimate=$0.09`, `requires_approval=true`, and `ended_at == approved_at = 2026-04-24T21:09:57`. Cross-check on `86f4378d-0645-449c-a676-28c28fc81f6f` (same tag, 13s wall-clock): `last_heartbeat - started_at = 13s`, also 1 turn / ~27k tokens / approval landed within 2ms. Identical agent work; wall-clock spread is ~6,000× because operator batch-cleared the approval queue at 21:09:5X UTC (25 runs ending within ~7s of each other). Wall-clock is therefore not a slow signal for sandboxed approval-required runs.

Current HEARTBEAT.md "Reasoning Framework" tier-3 prose: "Slow — run exceeded expected tokens or duration by > 50%". "Duration" is unqualified; natural reading is wall-clock.

Proposed edit: replace tier-3 line with — "3. **Slow** — run exceeded expected tokens or **work-duration** by > 50%. Work-duration = `last_heartbeat - started_at` (or equivalent agent-side span), NOT `ended_at - started_at`. When `resolved_config.requires_approval=true`, wall-clock includes operator approval latency and is not a slow signal. Also exclude candidates where `summary.turns_used <= 1` AND `summary.cost_estimate < $0.20` (a 1-turn cheap run is structurally not slow regardless of wall-clock)."

Expected delta: tier-3 picks no longer dominated by approval-queue artifacts. The current 25-run cluster falls out; future tier-3 picks reflect actual agent inefficiency.

Measurement plan: (a) 7 heartbeats from now (2026-05-01), grep RUN_LESSONS.md for any tier-3 lesson opened on a `requires_approval=true` run with `turns_used <= 1`. Expected count: 0. (b) When tier-3 next fires, the picked run should have `last_heartbeat - started_at` actually > 50% over expected.

Failure-mode check: (1) not polishing — concrete contamination affecting 25/98 runs in one window; (2) not sprawl — edit existing agent file; (3) not premature programmatic conversion — prose-to-prose; (4) not churn — clear baseline + delta; (5) not too-fast deprecation — improve, not prune; (6) in-lane — run-introspector observes, team-agent-optimizer implements (per RUN_LESSONS.md handoff convention); the underlying agent-manager `ended_at` semantics are explicitly NOT touched (correct as-is for audit); (7) not conversion-without-measurement — measurement plan above.

This is the second tier-contamination lesson in two heartbeats (after dec-1776984436121140045 / tier-1 `detectRateLimit` false-positives). They are additive (different tiers, different gates), not redundant — no supersession of yesterday's pending decision. If a third tier-contamination lesson surfaces, contrarian should consider `framework-update` for tier-signal-contamination as a standing failure mode.
